attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack essay, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'We can be sure... will get heavily used' is a firm forecast with no deadline and no threshold. The normalised proposition matches it.

contract.note: The plain reading (substantial, repeated, feature-specific use) is ordinary and fair. Refusing to count overall ChatGPT adoption as Deep Research use is reasonable.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure (Jan 2026). It says advanced features, Deep Research among them, are underused overall but used more by power and technical users. It gives no feature-specific scale, so it neither establishes nor rules out heavy use.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The only evidence is a company disclosure that mentions Deep Research use by power users and calls advanced features underused. It has no usage figures, reporting period or repeat-use data. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his essay.

semantics.note: 'Is going to make that problem worse' is a firm forecast. The 'because' clause is a stated mechanism, correctly kept as a qualifier rather than a condition. 'That problem' is fairly read as AI-generated garbage polluting the internet.

contract.note: Requiring a contribution attributable to Deep Research itself, not AI content in general, fits the claim's specific target. The contradiction bar is high but suits a forecast with no deadline.

evidence.note: NewsGuard's tracker shows AI content-farm pollution continuing, but does not attribute any of it to OpenAI Deep Research.
OpenAI's system card (company disclosure) reports a lower hallucination rate on a benchmark. It says nothing about public junk production, so it neither confirms nor rules out the forecast.
May 2026 preprint finds OpenAI Deep Research rarely cites user-generated content. Its poisoning experiments used other systems, so it does not show Deep Research adding junk to the public web.

reviews.rationale: This is a forecast with no deadline. No evidence item ties added public junk content to OpenAI Deep Research or to its speed or reach. The system card and preprint qualify the claim but do not exclude the predicted contribution. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his essay.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' language, with the scope 'virtually everything' preserved. The normalisation is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'virtually everything' as nearly all reports, and 'passing' as looking credible on first inspection, is the ordinary reading. Requiring representative user studies is demanding but fair for a population-wide claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no evidence items. The stated gaps say no representative study pairs first-impression credibility judgments of Deep Research reports with accuracy checks. With no deadline and no qualifying evidence, the forecast cannot be scored. The empty packet is a gap in the evidence, not a broken case.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. He mentions Unutmaz's recommendation, but the prediction itself is his.

semantics.note: 'Will start to use it' and 'inevitably errors will seep in... often undetected' are firm forecasts. The normalisation keeps both 'often' and 'undetected'.

contract.note: The result depends on how 'often' and 'undetected' are read; Marcus supplied no threshold for either. The contract's reading (a recurring pattern escaping pre-publication checks) is ordinary and fair to him.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed JMIR paper (July 2025). The authors tested Deep Research-generated reviews and annotated errors, which shows researchers using it experimentally. They say generative AI was not used to write the paper, so no errors entered the literature through it.

reviews.rationale: This is a forecast with no deadline. e1 shows some researcher use of Deep Research, in experiments. No evidence traces published errors to Deep Research, and no audit shows such errors recurrently escaping checks. The support condition is not met, and a finite search cannot contradict the claim.
